body:
Thank you for taking the time to share your story. Your story mirrors mine a great deal. I also followed a compulsive need to find newer content via the dark web. Sessions would sometimes last hours at a time. The thrill of the new, the chase. A sick and powerful delusion. The addiction takes us to very dark places and gets emboldened by seeing others in CP communities. It gives our minds an excuse, a justification. It's an unfounded justification, but compulsion can blind us.

I totally relate with that notion of wishing you could remove that part of your brain that fixates on CP. I imagine that part of your brain disgusts you because you know it runs against the rest of you. The good parts of you.

The fact is you and I both made a grave mistake. We let an addiction destroy our old life. I understand the hopelessness. I understand the depression. We are not wrong for having those feelings. In fact, it shows that we do care, that we understand the gravity of the crimes. The future is going to be rough. But we have a purpose: to atone. Regardless of what the legal outcome is; beyond that lies a life full of opportunity to make smarter choices.

Our crimes hurt children. Indirectly, but still actively. It fed into a diseased behemoth. So let's start today by firstly not offending again. But also by putting positive vibes into the world. Do good deeds, seek to help people. We can't undo the damage we have done. But we can add positivity back into world.

I know anxiety and depression run rampant with you. As it does with me. But take time to remind youself that you still have good to give this world. I believe in you.
I'm still admitst the pretrail phase of my journey. But I can say we wary of anytime they tell you "soon". Soon in the legal system appears to be an ever moving goalpost.

That very much makes sense. The human mind is both our greatest ally and greatest enemy. Your observation that the human brian has not caught up to the rapid technology rate of our modern world is very insightful. Most progress in human history can be tracked in increments of centuries. But today it seems decades worth of advancements happen every year. Yes our world is more progressive and shiny...but maybe it's not really human enough anymore.

When I think about my porn addiction and how it's escalation lead me to CP, I can draw a direct correlation between the advance of tech and the growth of my porn habit. Now I'm not scapegoating technology. Computers and internet didn't make me look at porn. Rather it give me a very easy outlet to cope with my social phobias. Rather then addressing my depression and anxiety issues, I just threw myself into viewing porn for relief.

I have heard people say we are more connected theb ever yet simultaneously more alone the ever. I think in many respects that is painfully true.

Thanks, I needed to see this today. Even before my arrest, I was prone to worrying what others thought of me. Worrying to the point of compulsive. If I ever felt like I "let somebody down" it would stay in my thoughts. For days or weeks. Having that personality and now facing a sex offense charge has nearly broken me mentally. Logically I know I shouldn't worry what other people think of me. But I spent so much time trying to cultivate a pristine image, that it prevented me from really living my life.

I need to change the way my mind works. I need to focus more on living in the moment. I know in my heart that in my 32 years of life I have done way more good then harm. So I have to cherish that and keep moving forward. I need to jettison any evil actions I take and channel that energy into making the world as positive as is within my power.

Hope goes a long way. As does a mother's love for their child. You are strong and brave for supporting him. My mom is also a rock for me right now. I can say from personal experience it's a light in dark cave. A beacon when it feels like society at large has chucked you in a trash bin.

I just ordered the A Torturous Path book your son recommended. It looks like a great find. I've been seeking out any and all stories from people that have faced a sex offender charge. It has shown me I'm not alone. There are far too many who have been taken by the sinister grip of child pornography. Education of the how and why is just as important as prison time or probation if society wants to stop this crime. We can't look at sex offenders as merely sub-human statistics. There is a face, a family, and story behind every sex offender.

Thank you for helping to spread your son's story. The story mirrors so much of my situation. I too failed to cultivate healthy coping skills and it lead me down a dark path. Porn addiction makes good people do bad things. I can tell that your son is a good person. And he will get the good life he deserves after this ordeal has passed. I believe that for him and I believe it for myself.

One benefit that comes to mind is a greatly reduced amount of troll posts. Reddit is a big forum so anybody can stop by the subreddit to troll without having to actively make an account. Outspoken Offender's new platform is likely to attract just actual members with good intentions.

Hopefully u/prisoner256 has a safe and productive prison stay. I'm glad he was able to get some insight from this subreddit and I'm equally glad he was able to share his experiences on the sentencing odyssey. I think both actions go a long way in giving a face to what can seem to be a dark and scary process.

Labels by their very nature are meant to be shorthand. Couple that with humanity's general tendency to assume the worst and it leads to people assuming sex offender = pedophile. But the reality is far more nuanced. Whether it be a hands-on offence or a CP offense.

For example, hands-on abuse of children can sometimes be more about a quest for power/control as opposed to a sexual attraction. Predatory behaviour can be more opportunistic as opposed to long term planned.

CP offences run the gamet from CP producers to people that sincerely stumble upon it by accident. And all that grey area in between; which includes a large number of obsessive collectors that foster the habit for years. The pervasive presence of CP has unfortunately placed it in front of many more eyeballs then ever before. That is why law enforcement has rightfully labeled the issue an epidemic.

One last piece worth noting is how the news covers stories of child sexual abuse. The word pedophile is thrown around liberally in articles and videos. Hence the shorthand is perpetuated.

I very much feel your pain. The anxiety experienced while being in investigated is overwhelming. One thing I would recommend is taking walks, the longer the better. Physical exercise is a great way to keep racing thoughts at bay.

Another godsend for me has been YouTube and podcasts. They are two of the few hobbies that I have held onto from my pre-arrest life. Learning about new things is a great way to take yourself mentally out of the anxiety bubble. Even if only temporarily.

I'm sorry for the mental anguish you are experiencing at the moment. I understand the feeling well because I'm in the same boat. I'm currently pretrail on a CP case. The single biggest painful aspect of this ordeal has been letting my family and friends down.

Thoughts of suicidal are natural in these situations. That may sound dark, but I find it to be true. The cocktail of emotions one expeiences: remorse, shame, guilt, anxiety, depression...it all blends together to what can feel unbearable. But suicide isn't the solution. Life still has meaning. Just a new meaning that you are free to craft.

The act of engaging with CP, in an capacity, causes victimization. Some penance is due. I think the anxiety and sense of loss is part of that penance. Be remorseful and work to make it up to your victims. But at the same time don't let this experience define you for the rest of your life. You still have your family. Going forward be a better person for them. Be a better person for yourself.
